description_nl: Locaties en contouren van alle rijksmonumenten in Nederland. Rijksmonumenten zijn gebouwen, objecten en terreinen die van nationaal belang zijn vanwege hun schoonheid, betekenis voor de wetenschap of cultuurhistorische waarde, beschermd onder de Erfgoedwet.
description_en: Locations and contours of all national listed monuments (rijksmonumenten) in the Netherlands. These are buildings, objects, and sites of national importance due to their beauty, scientific significance, or cultural-historical value, protected under the Heritage Act (Erfgoedwet).

provider.name_en: Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands
provider.role: Custodian of the national monument register (Rijksmonumentenregister)

rce_download_service.notes: Periodic download service. Files are Shapefile format in EPSG:28992.

pdok_ogc_api.notes: OGC API Features service hosted by PDOK. Returns GeoJSON in EPSG:4326 by default. Paginated (max 1000 per page). May be more current than the download service.

monument_register.notes: Public web interface for looking up individual monuments by number. Each monument's rijksurl field links directly to its register page.

license.notes: No restrictions stated in the Atom download feed. Dutch government open data.

crs.name: Amersfoort / RD New
crs.notes: Standard Dutch national coordinate reference system (Rijksdriehoekstelsel). Uses Oblique Stereographic projection with origin near Amersfoort. Units are metres.

rijksmonumentpunten.description: Point locations for all nationally listed monuments. Each feature represents one monument with its point location (centroid or address-derived coordinate).

columns.name: gml_parent
columns.description_en: GML identifier of the parent object. Used in GML source data to establish parent-child relationships. In this Shapefile export, this field is always null.
columns.notes: Always null in the current Shapefile export. Parent-child relationships are represented through the complex_nu field instead.

columns.name: gml_id
columns.description_en: Unique GML identifier for the point feature
columns.notes: Format: 'NationalListedMonumentPoints.NNNNN'. The numeric suffix is a sequential feature ID, NOT the monument number.

columns.name: rijksmonum
columns.description_nl: Uniek nummer waarmee het rijksmonument is geregistreerd in het Rijksmonumentenregister
columns.description_en: Unique national monument registration number. This is the primary key for looking up a monument in the national register.
columns.notes: Integer stored as Real due to Shapefile limitations. The key identifier used across all RCE systems. Used in the rijksurl to link to the monument register.

columns.name: complex_nu
columns.description_nl: Nummer van het complex waartoe dit monument behoort
columns.description_en: Number of the complex (group) to which this monument belongs. Multiple monuments can share the same complex number, indicating they form an ensemble (e.g., a church with its rectory, or a farm with its barn).
columns.notes: About 14,033 of 63,073 monuments (22%) belong to a complex. The complex number is itself a rijksmonumentnummer of one of the constituent monuments. Null for standalone monuments.

columns.name: juridische
columns.description_nl: De juridische status van het beschermde object
columns.description_en: Legal protection status of the monument
columns.notes: All features in this dataset have the value 'rijksmonument'. Other statuses (e.g., gemeentelijk monument / municipal monument) are maintained in separate datasets.

columns.name: aard_monum
columns.description_nl: De aard van het monument: archeologisch of onroerend gebouwd
columns.description_en: Nature/type of the monument: archaeological or built (immovable property)

archeologisch.description: Archaeological sites and terrain monuments (1,461 features)

onroerend gebouwd.description: Built structures — buildings, infrastructure, objects (61,612 features)

columns.name: herkomst
columns.description_nl: Bron waaruit de geometrie (puntlocatie) is afgeleid
columns.description_en: Source from which the point geometry was derived. Indicates which base registry or method was used to geocode the monument.

BAG.description: Derived from the Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen — the authoritative Dutch building and address registry. Most common source.

RCE dico.description: Geocoded using the RCE's own 'dico' geocoding tool

Bridgis.description: Geocoded using the commercial Bridgis service

BRK.description: Derived from the Basisregistratie Kadaster — the Dutch cadastral registration

AMR dico.description: Geocoded using the AMR geocoding tool (related to AMR/Archis archaeological data system)

GBKN.description: Derived from the Grootschalige Basiskaart van Nederland (now superseded by BGT)

BGT.description: Derived from the Basisregistratie Grootschalige Topografie

columns.notes: 83 features have null herkomst. The herkomst value reflects how accurate and current the point location is — BAG-derived points tend to be the most reliable.

columns.name: kwaliteit_
columns.description_nl: Aanduiding van de nauwkeurigheid van de puntlocatie
columns.description_en: Quality indicator for the point location accuracy

globaal.description: Approximate location — may be off by tens to hundreds of metres (37,881 features, 60%)

exact.description: Exact location — directly on or very close to the monument (21,041 features, 33%)

besluit.description: Location as specified in the official designation decree. Mainly used for archaeological monuments (4,151 features, 7%)

columns.notes: The field name is truncated from 'kwaliteit' to 'kwaliteit_' due to the Shapefile 10-character field name limit.

columns.name: hoofdcateg
columns.description_nl: Hoofdcategorie van het monument volgens het RCE-classificatiesysteem
columns.description_en: Main category of the monument according to the RCE classification system
columns.notes: The (N) suffix on 'Archeologie (N)' is a legacy classification code. 1 feature has null hoofdcategorie. The field name is truncated from 'hoofdcategorie' due to Shapefile limits.

columns.name: subcategor
columns.description_nl: Subcategorie van het monument, nadere specificatie van de hoofdcategorie
columns.description_en: Subcategory of the monument, further specifying the main category. Some subcategories include a legacy letter-number code in parentheses.
columns.notes: 66 distinct values. The letter-number codes in parentheses (e.g., K, M, C, D, N1) are legacy codes from an older classification system. Field name truncated from 'subcategorie' due to Shapefile limits.

columns.name: rijksurl
columns.description_nl: Directe link naar de pagina van dit monument in het online Rijksmonumentenregister
columns.description_en: Direct URL to this monument's page in the online National Monument Register. Provides full details including address, description, images, and designation history.

columns.name: geom
columns.description_en: An additional geometry field present in the GML source data, stored as a string in the Shapefile export. Always null in this dataset.
columns.notes: Artifact of the GML-to-Shapefile conversion. Can be safely ignored. Not present in the contours layer.

rijksmonumentcontouren.description: Contour/outline geometries for a subset of nationally listed monuments. Primarily covers archaeological sites and a subset of built monuments that have surveyed boundary polygons.

data_quality_issue.summary: Geometry appears corrupt or empty in the Shapefile export
data_quality_issue.details: ogrinfo reports the geometry type as Point with an extent of (0,0)-(0,0), despite the gml_id values containing 'NationalListedMonumentPolygons' (e.g., 'NationalListedMonumentPolygons.10001'). The .shp file is only 49 KB for 4,149 features, far too small for polygon data. The attribute data in the .dbf (9.6 MB) appears intact. This suggests the polygon geometries were lost or corrupted during the GML-to-Shapefile conversion by the data provider.
data_quality_issue.recommendation: Use the PDOK OGC API to obtain contour polygons with intact geometry: https://api.pdok.nl/rce/beschermde-gebieden-cultuurhistorie/ogc/v1/collections/rijksmonumentcontouren/items
data_quality_issue.workaround: The points layer covers all 63,073 monuments including those in the contours layer. The rijksmonumentnummer can be used to join contour attributes if polygon geometry is obtained from the PDOK API.

columns.name: gml_parent
columns.description_en: GML identifier of the parent object. Always null in this export.

columns.name: gml_id
columns.description_en: Unique GML identifier for the contour feature
columns.notes: Format: 'NationalListedMonumentPolygons.NNNNN'. Note: 'Polygons' in the ID confirms these should be polygon geometries.

columns.name: rijksmonum
columns.description_en: Unique national monument registration number. Same identifier as in the points layer, can be used for joining.

columns.name: complex_nu
columns.description_en: Complex group number (see points layer documentation)

columns.name: juridische
columns.description_en: Legal protection status — always 'rijksmonument'

columns.name: aard_monum
columns.description_en: Nature of the monument: 'archeologisch' or 'onroerend gebouwd'

columns.name: herkomst
columns.description_en: Source from which the contour geometry was derived

columns.name: kwaliteit_
columns.description_en: Quality indicator for the contour geometry accuracy

columns.name: hoofdcateg
columns.description_en: Main category (see points layer for full enumeration)

columns.name: subcategor
columns.description_en: Subcategory (see points layer for full enumeration)

columns.name: rijksurl
columns.description_en: Direct URL to the monument's register page

rijksmonumentcontouren.notes: The contours layer does NOT have the extra 'geom' string field that appears in the points layer. All 1,461 archaeological monuments have contours; only 2,688 of the ~61,600 built monuments have contours (~4.4%).

category_classification_system.description: The RCE uses a two-level classification system: hoofdcategorie (main category) and subcategorie (subcategory). Some categories and subcategories include legacy alphanumeric codes in parentheses from an older classification system.

context.what: A Rijksmonument (national monument) is a building, object, or site in the Netherlands that has been designated as being of national significance for its beauty, scientific importance, or cultural-historical value. The designation is a legal protection status under the Erfgoedwet (Heritage Act, 2016, succeeding the Monumentenwet 1988).
context.scale: The Netherlands has approximately 63,000 rijksmonumenten. Amsterdam alone has about 8,000. The majority (98%) are 'onroerend gebouwd' (built structures); about 2% are archaeological sites.
context.implications: A Rijksmonument designation means the owner must obtain a permit (omgevingsvergunning) for any modifications to the monument. Owners may be eligible for subsidies and tax benefits for maintenance and restoration. Demolition is generally prohibited.
context.governance: The Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed (RCE) maintains the register and advises on designations. The Minister of Education, Culture and Science makes the formal designation decisions. Municipalities are responsible for enforcement via building permits.
context.complexes: About 22% of monuments belong to a 'complex' — a group of related monuments that together form an ensemble. Examples include a church with its associated rectory and churchyard wall, or a country estate with its main house, gardens, and outbuildings. The complex_nu field links these together.

related_datasets.name: Beschermde stads- en dorpsgezichten
related_datasets.description: Areas (rather than individual buildings) designated for their historical character. Available from the same RCE/PDOK source.

related_datasets.name: UNESCO Werelderfgoed
related_datasets.description: Sites with international UNESCO designation. Some rijksmonumenten are also part of UNESCO World Heritage Sites (e.g., Canal Ring of Amsterdam, Defence Line of Amsterdam).

related_datasets.name: Gemeentelijke monumenten
related_datasets.description: Monuments protected at the municipal level (estimated 50,000–100,000 nationwide). Maintained by individual municipalities, not available as a single national dataset.
